svg.title: Ishikari: full animated flow
svg.text: Asks the user only in step 1. Answering approves the whole run, merge to main included. Never pushes: main moves only by the finisher's fast-forward.

g.text: one live agent, run by the skill
~/.ishikari/<repo>-<hash>/boards/ - for you, no ant reads it

svg.text: gets each answer as a message

g.text: blocker set: stop it, show reason, stop.
report written: stop it with TaskStop;
the report is all later ants read.
and every task after a dropped one.
A dropped task's branch is kept.

svg.text: in a scratch copy, tests once
finds why a bug is still open
after a failed fix, writes the

g.text: Max 3 tries on a bug and
Bugs or waiting: new build round,
round from moved main. Then req done.
turned into questions for the next task
end of build: every task and bug, once
The task reaches the live Investigator Ant.
It asks the user up to 4 questions a round; answers come back as messages.
Nothing unclear: it writes investigation_report.md, then stops.
Plan workflow: the Add Requirement Ant reads the report.
Worker Ants start in parallel, one worktree each, max 5.
Built: the build script starts this task's inspector at once.
Fail, round 1: a worker builds the inspector's own fix plan.
Built: the build script starts this task's inspector at once.
Still open after round 1: the script hands the bug to the Detective Ant.
Detective's fix plan goes back to a Worker Ant.
Built: the build script starts this task's inspector at once.
Fix re-inspected: pass, once every task is checked.
They work combined: the main session approves them for the Merger, no review.
Merged (build's trial merge reused if it fits); the Verifier checks each task landed.
Verified: the Janitor plans a cleanup of this run's mess.
A Worker Ant builds the cleanup now, on top of the merge.
Built: the build script starts this task's inspector at once.
Philosopher critiques alongside; both end, scratch takes the cleanup; the Finisher moves main.
Done. Report once: what landed, dropped tasks, critiques, cleanup plan.
